subsystems.name: Chassis cell
subsystems.role: the host organism that will do the chemistry — commonly E. coli, yeast or a mammalian cell line.
parts: bacterial cells (fast, cheap, no complex sugars)
mammalian cells (for antibodies and complex human proteins)

subsystems.name: Genetic circuit
subsystems.role: the designed DNA that tells the cell what to make and when.

subsystems.name: DNA construction
subsystems.role: makes and assembles the designed sequences.

subsystems.name: Genome editing and evolution
subsystems.role: puts the design into the cell and improves it.

subsystems.name: Fermentation
subsystems.role: grows the cells at scale under controlled conditions.

subsystems.name: Downstream processing
subsystems.role: separates the product from the broth at high purity.

buildSteps.title: Choose the chassis
buildSteps.detail: Pick the host whose metabolism and safety profile best suit the target molecule — a bacterium for a simple protein, a yeast for a plant-derived compound, a mammalian cell for a glycosylated antibody.

buildSteps.title: Design the pathway
buildSteps.detail: Map the enzyme steps from a cheap feedstock to the target, then rewrite the genes for the chosen host's codon usage and balance expression so no intermediate accumulates to toxic levels.

buildSteps.title: Synthesise the DNA
buildSteps.detail: Short strands are chemically made and joined into longer constructs, then sequence-verified before use.

buildSteps.title: Install it in the cell
buildSteps.detail: The circuit is carried on a plasmid or inserted into the chromosome using targeted nucleases, with markers used to find successful edits.

buildSteps.title: Select and re-engineer
buildSteps.detail: Automated screens test thousands of variants; the best producers are re-designed and cycled through further rounds, sometimes with laboratory evolution to improve tolerance and yield.

buildSteps.title: Scale the fermentation
buildSteps.detail: The winning strain is grown from a small vial up through progressively larger vessels to production bioreactors, where feed, oxygen and temperature are tuned to keep it productive.

buildSteps.title: Recover and purify
buildSteps.detail: Cells are separated, the product captured and purified by chromatography and filtration, then tested for identity, potency and contamination before release.

buildSteps.title: For a fully synthetic cell
buildSteps.detail: The theoretical route is different: assemble a chemically synthesised minimal genome, transplant it into an emptied cell envelope, and add only the genes the cell needs to live and produce the target.

prerequisites.why: designs are now limited by cost and turnaround, not by the ability to write sequences.
targeted nucleases let engineers change specific genes instead of hoping for random mutation.
knowing which genes are active under production conditions is what makes redesigns rational rather than trial-and-error.
a functioning cell with a reduced synthetic genome has been built, but the rules for which genes are essential are still incompletely understood.
a strain that works in a flask fails at scale unless mixing, oxygen transfer, heat removal and downstream recovery are solved.
cells engineered to outcompete wild organisms need safeguards so they cannot escape or persist outside the plant.

pathway.milestone: engineered microbes already make insulin, enzymes and other proteins at commercial scale
pathway.unlocks: a proven industrial base for fermentation and purification.

pathway.milestone: complex molecules and new chemistries made in cells instead of from petrochemicals or plant extraction
pathway.unlocks: cheaper, more reliable supply of drugs and specialty chemicals.

pathway.milestone: cell-free and minimal-cell systems with defined, non-living or reduced genomes
pathway.unlocks: faster design cycles and fewer side reactions from unnecessary metabolism.

pathway.milestone: programmable cells and consortia running on waste or captured CO₂
pathway.unlocks: bulk chemicals and fuels made biologically at cost parity with fossil routes.
